intro.title: Build money currency branded type
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a branded type to represent money currency, ensuring that values like 'USD' or 'EUR' are treated as distinct types to prevent mixing them accidentally. You'll learn about TypeScript's type branding technique, which adds a unique property to a base type to create a new, incompatible type. The main constructs involved are type aliases, literal types, and intersection types. By the end, you'll have a practical, type-safe way to handle different currencies in financial applications.
intro.usecase: In financial applications like banking dashboards or e-commerce platforms, ensuring currency values are never confused with other numeric data is critical. For example, when displaying account balances, processing payments, or calculating taxes, using branded types prevents accidentally mixing USD amounts with EUR amounts or treating monetary values as simple numbers. This pattern appears in transaction forms where currency conversion must be type-safe, in reporting panels that aggregate different currencies, and in API responses that must guarantee currency integrity throughout the application.
